title: New Study: Nicotine Patch Slows Memory Loss in Mild Cognitive Impairment; Similar Study in PD on the Horizon | Parkinson's Disease
abstract: # New Study: Nicotine Patch Slows Memory Loss in Mild Cognitive Impairment; Similar Study in PD on the Horizon. This week, research published in *Neurology*, the medical journal of the American Academy of Neurology, found that a nicotine patch may improve the memory loss common in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), a condition that is often a precursor to Alzheimer’s disease. MJFF is funding a clinical study set to begin this spring called NIC-PD that will begin to look into the disease modifying potential of a nicotine patch, as well as its potential effects on the non-motor and in particular, cognitive features of PD. While the recent study results on MCI are encouraging, it is important to note the relatively small scale nature of the study, and that the use of nicotine patches as a treatment for any neurological disease is still in the early stages of investigation.
